module_title: Basics of Heat, Temperature, and Heat Transfer
introduction: Heat and Temperature are often confused in daily life, but in physics, they are distinct. Heat is a form of energy, while temperature is the measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

core_concepts.title: Heat vs. Temperature
core_concepts.description:
1. Heat: A form of energy that flows from a hotter body to a colder body. SI Unit: Joule (J). 
2. Temperature: The measure of average kinetic energy of molecules. SI Unit: Kelvin (K).

core_concepts.title: Temperature Scales
core_concepts.description:
There are three main scales: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), and Kelvin (K). 
Formula to convert: $\frac{C}{5} = \frac{F - 32}{9} = \frac{K - 273}{5}$. 
Important: $-40^\circ$ is the temperature where Celsius and Fahrenheit scales read exactly the same.

core_concepts.title: Modes of Heat Transfer
core_concepts.description:
1. Conduction: Heat transfer through direct contact without movement of particles (e.g., heating a metal rod). 
2. Convection: Heat transfer through the actual mass movement of fluid molecules (e.g., boiling water, sea breezes). 
3. Radiation: Heat transfer through electromagnetic waves requiring NO medium (e.g., heat from the Sun reaching Earth).

important_entities.name: Absolute Zero
important_entities.significance: This is the lowest theoretically possible temperature in the universe. At Absolute Zero, all molecular motion completely stops. Note: There is no negative temperature on the Kelvin scale.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Heat doesn't always flow to 'colder' objects
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Heat flows based purely on TEMPERATURE DIFFERENCE, not on the total heat energy. A spark from a firework has high temperature but very little total heat, yet heat will still flow from the spark to your skin (lower temperature).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Conduction = Touch, Convection = Travel, Radiation = Ray
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Touch (direct contact in solids), Travel (molecules moving in liquids/gases), Ray (electromagnetic waves through vacuum).

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent SSC question: 'How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?' Answer: Radiation.
